title: Shot by Kern
format: Hardcover with dust jacket and DVD

description.main: Some 300 photographs Richard Kern made around the world for his Vice video series Shot by Kern, published by Taschen in 2013 as a trilingual hardcover edited by Dian Hanson, with an hour-long DVD scored by Thurston Moore.
description.extended:
Shot by Kern gathers some 300 photographs Richard Kern made on the road for his Vice video series of the same name, still pictures from sessions that viewers had only ever seen as video.

The series began on Vice's video site VBS in 2007, when editor Jesse Pearson sent Kern out of New York to photograph women in their own cities. Over the following seven years he worked in eighteen countries, from Brazil and Mexico to Poland and New Zealand, with a Vice crew filming each shoot. Taschen published the photographs in 2013 as a 288-page hardcover edited by Dian Hanson, with text in English, French and German and an interview with Kern by Pearson. The pictures are grouped by recurring subject, including prescription drugs, phones, beds, upskirts and bathroom grooming. As with Kern's earlier Taschen book Action, a DVD is bound in, an hour of video shot and edited by Kern with music by Thurston Moore.

Kern, born in North Carolina in 1954 and based in New York since 1979, made the short films of the Cinema of Transgression in the 1980s and turned to still photography in the 1990s. His books include New York Girls (1995), Model Release (2000), Action (2007) and Looker (2008), along with many small zines.
description.artist_bio: Richard Kern (b. 1954, North Carolina) has lived and worked in New York since 1979. His 1980s short films are central to the Cinema of Transgression; since the 1990s he has worked almost entirely in still photography, publishing New York Girls, Model Release, Action, Looker and many zines.

notes: Shelf: Araki / Kern.
